page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU virtual server instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor architecture. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 188.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance operates under the QEMU hypervisor and does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores placing the instance in the top 25%. The AMD EPYC processor demonstrates strong capabilities in cryptographic operations, physics simulations, and extended instruction execution, as evidenced by high Passmark CPU scores. Memory performance is balanced, showing strong write bandwidth for large blocks alongside average read bandwidth. In database workloads, the ccx63 achieves strong results, processing 64.55 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring highly in Passmark database operations.

Given its dedicated resource allocation and balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ccx63 is highly efficient for workloads requiring sustained CPU performance without virtualization overhead. It is well-suited for software compilation, database hosting, and text or image processing. Additionally, the instance shows top-tier performance in small-scale language model text generation, making it viable for lightweight AI inference tasks. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and local NVMe storage offers a highly cost-effective profile for resource-dense, multi-threaded enterprise applications.
